title: Thessaly
capsule: Following the Fourth Crusade's dismemberment of Byzantium, Thessaly emerged as an independent despotate under John I Doukas from around 1271, extending its authority westward into Acarnania and Aetolia. John I's successors Constantine and John II Doukas maintained a precarious autonomy that included fending off Byzantine reconquest attempts; the Catalan Company raided and occupied parts of Thessaly between 1306 and 1310, carving out the Duchy of Neopatria from its southern reaches in 1319. After John II died in 1318 without organizing a succession, Byzantine Emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos completed the reconquest of northern Thessaly by 1332, and the region fell to Ottoman control around 1393.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The extent of the Thessalian despotate is reconstructed from Byzantine chronicles and Catalan administrative records; the western extension into Acarnania and Aetolia was ephemeral and imprecisely delimited.
